update.title: Updates
update.installing: Installing — the application restarts when it is done.
update.notInstalled: This is a development build, not an installed application: there is no installed copy for an update to replace.
update.autoHelp: Checks for updates when SevenShell starts. The request contains no personal data. You can also check manually.
update.centreHelp: The release channel: what is published, and what can be done about it.
update.publishedOver: The published version is {version}; the installed version is {current}.
update.ready: Version {version} has been downloaded. Restart to update.

support.title: Support information
support.description: Attach this to a bug report so the environment is known without a round of questions.

leaving.title: Close the settings?
leaving.message: Some changes have not been saved yet. Save them, discard them, or stay on this page.

sessionReopen.focus: Go to the tab that is open

schemes.sourceHostHint: The pane is dressed by the colours the window is wearing.
schemes.sourceCustomHint: The pane wears a published scheme of its own.

description.dark: The scheme the terminal wears while it is dark.
description.light: The scheme the terminal wears while it is light.

schemes.backgroundHint: The whole look replaces the background and text as well. Only the ANSI colours keeps the pane matching the window and changes what ls, git and editors print.

profileRemove.title: Remove saved scheme
profileRemove.message: Remove “{name}”? The terminal keeps the colours it is wearing; only the saved answer is deleted.

import.title: Import colour schemes
import.hint: Paste an Xresources block, a Windows Terminal JSON scheme, an iTerm2 .itermcolors file, or any JSON scheme with sixteen colours.
import.empty: That text is not a colour scheme with sixteen colours.

remove.title: Remove scheme
remove.message: Remove “{name}”? Terminals wearing it fall back to the interface palette.

highlights.modeBackgroundHint: A tint behind the word; the terminal's own text colour stays.
highlights.modeTextHint: The match itself takes the rule's colour, with no block.
highlights.hint: A rule marks every occurrence in the terminal, including output already on screen.
highlights.tooLong: A pattern may be at most {max} characters.
highlights.invalidRegex: That is not a valid regular expression.
highlights.removeMessage: Remove “{pattern}”? The marks it made disappear with it.

words.hint: Words suggested after a command. Built-in words ship with every installation; add tools this version does not know here.
words.builtinHint: Built-in rows are read-only. Add a row with the same command and word to override one.
words.restoreMessage: All custom words are deleted; built-in words are untouched. This cannot be undone.
words.noteHint: Shown beside the word instead of the built-in description.
words.spaceInvalid: A command and a word are one word each: the command line is split on spaces before anything is looked up.
words.saveFailed: The word could not be written.

layouts.introHint: What this is and how a first connection goes. No host names, no counts, no history.
layouts.workspaceHint: What the library holds, the hosts used last, and the actions that start something.

appLayout.separatedHint: Clear panel separation with block-style tabs.
appLayout.classicHint: Continuous tab bar with compact panel headers.

tabLayout.scrollHint: Tabs scroll horizontally in one row when overflowing.
tabLayout.wrapHint: Tabs wrap to multiple rows to show all at once.

themeMode.title: Interface theme
themeMode.summary: Follow the system, or keep to one of the two palettes.
themeMode.help: Following the system keeps changing with it while the application is open. A theme chosen outright is written down at once, so a restart opens the way it was left.

terminalTheme.title: Terminal colours
terminalTheme.summary: The palette the terminal itself draws in.
terminalTheme.help: A dark terminal in a light interface is a common choice, so the two are decided separately. Either way the sixteen ANSI colours come from the same palette, tuned to be readable on its own background.

language.title: Language
language.summary: The language the interface is written in.
language.help: Until a language is chosen the system's applies. Once one is chosen it stays — even on a machine that is set to something else.

colorTheme.title: Colour theme
colorTheme.summary: The colour the interface is made of, in either of the two themes.
colorTheme.help: Overrides the accent and terminal colours; light and dark mode stay independent.

uiScale.title: Interface scale
uiScale.summary: Draws the whole interface larger, inside the same window.
uiScale.help: Scales text, borders and the terminal grid without changing the window size.

homeContent.title: Home content
homeContent.summary: Which of the two pages is drawn with nothing open.
homeContent.help: The introduction explains the first connection. The workspace overview shows saved sessions, recent hosts and common actions.

appLayout.title: Interface layout
appLayout.summary: How much of the window is the thing being looked at.
appLayout.help: Separated gives each area its own frame. Classic joins the tabs into one bar and uses less space.

tabPlacement.title: Tab bar position
tabPlacement.summary: Side tab bars scroll vertically; multi-row wrapping applies only above or below content.
tabPlacement.help: Where the tab bar sits. Horizontal uses vertical space; vertical uses width and shows more names.

tabGroupMode.title: Group by
tabGroupMode.summary: Grouping affects only the displayed order.
tabGroupMode.help: Group tabs by session, or keep one continuous row. Settings and batch tabs stay after all groups.

tabSortMode.title: Sort by
tabSortMode.summary: Sorting affects only the displayed order; dragging is available in manual order.
tabSortMode.help: Manual order can be changed by dragging. Opening order and name order are read-only and follow the tabs.

tabMaxWidth.title: Maximum tab width
tabMaxWidth.summary: Limit the maximum width of horizontal tabs, truncating long titles with ellipsis. Hover to view the full title.
tabMaxWidth.help: Maximum width of a horizontal tab. Longer names are truncated and shown in full on hover. Vertical tabs use the column width.

background.title: Background image
background.summary: Set an image behind the whole app. Cards and dialogs stay opaque for readability.
background.help: The image is copied into the app's data folder. Transparency applies to panels and the window frame, not to cards or dialogs.

showTrayIcon.title: Show tray/menu bar icon
showTrayIcon.summary: When disabled, no icon is shown, but closing the window still hides 7Shell in the background as before.
showTrayIcon.help: Keep a tray icon. When enabled, closing the window hides it and the tray icon brings it back. When disabled, closing quits the app.

quitOnClose.title: Quit when closing window
quitOnClose.summary: When enabled, clicking the close button exits 7Shell completely instead of hiding it to the tray.
quitOnClose.help: When off, closing hides the window and keeps sessions running (requires the tray icon). When on, closing quits. Unsaved work is confirmed first.

tabLayout.title: Tab bar overflow
tabLayout.summary: What the tabs do when they no longer fit in one row.
tabLayout.help: One scrolling row, or wrapped rows that show every tab. Wrapping uses more height; scrolling keeps the panel height.

cornerStyle.title: Corner style
cornerStyle.summary: How round the corners of everything are.
cornerStyle.help: Corner style applies to the whole window. The buttons above preview each option.

uiFont.title: Interface font
uiFont.summary: The family the rest of the window is drawn in.
uiFont.help: Uses a font stack: if the first family is unavailable, the next one is used. Terminal font is set separately.

terminalFont.title: Terminal font
terminalFont.summary: The family the terminal's text is drawn in.
terminalFont.help: Fixed-width fonts are listed first. Changes apply to open terminals immediately.

terminalPreview.title: Live preview
terminalPreview.summary: A live preview of the terminal settings.
terminalPreview.help: A live preview of the terminal's font, spacing and palette as the settings below change.

terminalFontSize.title: Text size
terminalFontSize.summary: How large the terminal draws its text, in pixels.
terminalFontSize.help: Terminal font size in pixels. Open terminals redraw and reflow immediately.

terminalFontWeight.title: Text weight
terminalFontWeight.summary: How heavy the terminal's regular text is.
terminalFontWeight.help: The weight the shell's own text is drawn at. Bold text uses its own weight, set separately.

terminalBoldFontWeight.title: Bold weight
terminalBoldFontWeight.help: Some palettes draw bold and regular nearly alike. A heavier bold, or bright ANSI colours, is what keeps emphasis visible.

terminalLineHeight.title: Line height
terminalLineHeight.summary: The distance between lines, as a multiple of the font's height.
terminalLineHeight.help: Higher values give a line more room; lower values fit more lines in the same panel. The terminal reflows as it changes.

terminalLetterSpacing.title: Letter spacing
terminalLetterSpacing.help: Zero leaves the font's own spacing. Negative values pull characters together; positive values space them out. The grid is measured again as it changes.

terminalPaddingX.title: Horizontal padding
terminalPaddingX.summary: The room between the text and the panel's left and right edges.
terminalPaddingX.help: Keeps a full-width line off the frame. The column count is measured again when this changes.

terminalPaddingY.title: Vertical padding
terminalPaddingY.summary: The room above and below the text.
terminalPaddingY.help: Breathing space between a block of output and the panel's edges.

terminalCursorStyle.title: Cursor shape
terminalCursorStyle.summary: The shape that marks where typing goes.
terminalCursorStyle.help: Block, bar or underline. Shown while the terminal has the keyboard; the shape it takes without focus is a setting of its own.

terminalCursorBlink.title: Blinking cursor
terminalCursorBlink.help: A steady cursor is easier to follow in a recording or on a projector; a blinking one is easier to find after looking away.

terminalCursorInactive.title: Unfocused cursor
terminalCursorInactive.summary: What the cursor looks like while the window does not have the keyboard.
terminalCursorInactive.help: Outline keeps the cell marked without pretending it is taking input. Hidden removes it entirely.

terminalBoldBright.title: Bright bold text
terminalBoldBright.summary: Draw bold text in the bright half of the ANSI palette.
terminalBoldBright.help: On by default. Turning it off leaves weight as the only difference between bold and regular, which helps in palettes where the two colours are nearly the same.

terminalMinContrast.title: Minimum contrast
terminalMinContrast.summary: The lowest contrast ratio the terminal accepts before it adjusts the text colour.
terminalMinContrast.help: One leaves the palette exactly as designed. Higher values trade an exact scheme for readability; 4.5 is the usual reading baseline.

terminalSchemes.title: Terminal colour schemes
terminalSchemes.summary: A published scheme for the terminal, or the colours of the interface.
terminalSchemes.help: A scheme brings its own background, text and sixteen ANSI colours, one for each half of the terminal's light/dark setting. Leaving the source on the interface palette keeps the pane matching the window.

terminalHighlights.title: Keyword highlights
terminalHighlights.summary: Mark words in terminal output wherever they appear.
terminalHighlights.help: Rules apply to every open terminal, including output already on screen. A rule can be a plain word or a regular expression; the display mode decides whether the mark is a tint behind the word or the word's own colour.

sessionLayout.title: Opening a session
sessionLayout.summary: A terminal on its own, or with the files under it.
sessionLayout.help: Shows the file browser under the terminal and follows directory changes. Can be toggled per tab.

sessionReopen.title: A session that is already open
sessionReopen.summary: What the session list's menu does with one: ask, open another tab, or go to the tab that is there.
sessionReopen.help: Applies to Open terminal in the menu. Remember my choice stores the answer here; clicking a session row is unchanged.

monitor.title: Host monitor
monitor.summary: A panel beside the workspace: load, memory, network and file systems.
monitor.help: Shows load, memory, network and disks for the host of the current terminal, sampled every two seconds over its connection. Hidden means no sampling.

filesLayout.title: File browser
filesLayout.summary: A tree beside the list, or the list alone.
filesLayout.help: The tree opens the branches leading to the current directory, so the two panes never disagree about where that is.

packed.title: Packed transfer
packed.summary: Move a folder as one archive, made and opened on the way.
packed.help: Folders are packed on one side and unpacked on the other. Single files are transferred directly. Packing requires tar on the host.

commandCompletion.title: Command completion
commandCompletion.summary: Offer what this application knows while a command is being typed.
commandCompletion.help: Suggests commands, saved lines, history and paths as you type. Tab or the arrow keys select a suggestion; Enter inserts it, and Enter again runs the line. With nothing selected, Enter runs the line as typed. Escape closes the list; Alt+/ reopens it.

lines.output: ● nginx.service — A high performance web server
lines.warning: warning: 3 restarts in the last hour
lines.error: error: unit nginx.service entered failed state

password.title: Master password
password.help: Changes the vault password and re-encrypts the file. The current password is required even while the vault is unlocked.
password.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
password.same: The new password is the current one.
password.changed: The vault now opens with the new password.

lock.title: Lock the vault
lock.help: Drops the derived key and the decrypted document. Open terminals keep running — they are authenticated already — and the unlock screen comes back.

archives.title: Archived vaults
archives.help: Vaults that were moved aside, listed by name. One can be tried, switched to, or read into the vault that is open.

policy.title: Policy matrix
policy.description: What unattended work may do without a person: batches, containers, clusters and agent tool calls. Typing in a terminal is not governed by these rules — the person at the keyboard is the decision.
policy.mostRestrictive: Every matching layer applies and the strictest action decides (allow < ask < deny). A group, host or directory rule can tighten the global rule and never loosen it.
policy.normalized: Allow is raised to Ask for destructive and catastrophic actions: those two always stop for a person, so these rules decide where the question is asked, not whether it is.

groups.title: Group exceptions
groups.hint: Keyed by the session group's id.

hosts.title: Host exceptions
hosts.hint: A host name, or host:port for one port only.

directories.title: Directory exceptions
directories.hint: A remote path prefix. / matches every path, and matching is on path boundaries only, so /srv does not cover /srv-old.

policy.applied: Applied. Unattended actions follow these rules.

audit.title: Policy audit
audit.description: The matrix's most recent decisions, read from the trail on disk. The newest is last.
audit.empty: No decision has been recorded yet.
audit.failed: The trail could not be read.

commands.hint: The lines that have been kept, and the short text that brings each one up in the command line. This is the same library the panel under a terminal edits.
commands.saveFailed: The library could not be written.
commands.prefixInvalid: A trigger is one word, so it cannot contain a space.
commands.restoreMessage: The library is cleared, including added commands and groups, and the built-in lines are restored. This cannot be undone.

shortcuts.hint: Click Change, then press the combination to use instead. Escape leaves the key as it is, and a key that is no longer wanted can be unbound.

actions.uploadClipboard: Upload the files on the clipboard
actions.completionAccept: Take the row the arrows are on

knownHosts.empty: No host key has been trusted on this device yet.
knownHosts.forgetMessage: The key for {host} is forgotten. The next connection to it asks again, and nothing else changes.

keys.empty: No key yet. Import one, or make one here.
keys.makeHint: It is made on this machine and kept in the vault. The public line is the half that goes on a server.
keys.publicHint: Paste it into authorized_keys on the server.
keys.forgetMessage: The key material for {name} is removed. The {count} session(s) using it cannot connect until another key or password is set.
